description: Fig. 1 is a three-panel composite figure mixing a process schematic, a CALPHAD phase-fraction plot and a dilatometry curve. (a) Temperature-time schematic of the thermomechanical route after casting: Homogenization 1100 °C 2hr, Hot forging + air cooling, Hot rolling 1100 °C 2hr (with an intermediate reheating step), water quenching, Intercritical Annealing 750 °C for 5-180 min, then air cooling. (b) Thermo-Calc equilibrium phase-fraction plot: y-axis "Volume fraction of all phase" 0-1.0, x-axis "Temperature (°C)" with ticks 200-1600; legend lists BCC_A2, FCC_A1, LIQUID, KAPPA_E21, Cementite, M23C6, CUB_A13, FE8SI2C, CBCC_A12. BCC_A2 falls from ~0.9 to a minimum ~0.5 near 900 °C, rises to a maximum ~0.95 near 1370 °C and vanishes ~1450 °C; FCC_A1 appears near 550 °C, peaks ~0.53 around 950-1000 °C and drops to ~0.1 by 1350 °C; LIQUID rises steeply above ~1380 °C. (c) Dilatometry "Change in Length" (no unit printed) from -50 to 200 versus Temperature, with two near-coincident curves labelled "5 min. holding time" (black) and "15 min. holding time" (red); a black ellipse marks a slight deviation at ~600 °C. Together the panels justify selecting 750 °C as the intercritical annealing temperature and show negligible transformation-related contraction.
measured_quantities: change in length (arbitrary units; no unit printed)

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a Temperature (°C) versus Time schematic that sequences Homogenization (1100 °C, 2hr) → Hot forging + air cooling → Hot rolling (1100 °C, 2hr) → water quenching → Intercritical Annealing (750 °C, 5-180 Min) → air cooling.
The intercritical annealing step in panel (a) is annotated with the temperature 750 °C and a duration range of 5-180 Min.

Panel (b) is labelled 'Volume fraction of all phase' on the y-axis (0.0 to 1.0) against 'Temperature (°C)' on the x-axis, and its legend contains nine phases: BCC_A2, FCC_A1, LIQUID, KAPPA_E21, Cementite, M23C6, CUB_A13, FE8SI2C and CBCC_A12.
In panel (b) the BCC_A2 curve passes through a minimum of about 0.5 near 900 °C and reaches a maximum just below 1400 °C before dropping sharply toward zero at roughly 1450 °C.

In panel (b) the FCC_A1 (austenite) curve is essentially zero below ~550 °C, rises to a broad maximum of about 0.5 near 950-1000 °C and falls back to roughly 0.1 at 1350 °C, defining the duplex BCC_A2 + FCC_A1 region.

In panel (b) the LIQUID curve only becomes non-zero above ~1380 °C and rises steeply, reaching 1.0 at about 1500 °C; all other listed phases (KAPPA_E21, Cementite, M23C6, CUB_A13, FE8SI2C, CBCC_A12) remain at or very near zero volume fraction over the plotted range.

Panel (c) plots 'Change in Length' (y-axis, -50 to 200, no unit printed) against Temperature (°C) and contains two curves labelled '5 min. holding time' (black) and '15 min. holding time' (red) that lie almost on top of one another.
A black ellipse in panel (c) marks a slight deviation between/along the curves at approximately 600 °C during heating and cooling; no other significant hump or contraction is visible.
The caption states that (c) is the dilatometry heating-cooling curve of the hot forged sample.
The caption states that (b) is a Thermo-Calc equilibrium phase fraction plot and (a) a schematic of thermomechanical processing after casting.
The text states the Thermo-Calc calculation used database TCFE9 and that the duplex ferrite (δ) + austenite (γ) region spans approximately 650 °C to 1350 °C.
The text states that based on the dual-phase region an intercritical annealing temperature of 750 °C was chosen for the designed steel.

The text states that the dilatometry curve shows no significant deviation/hump in change in length during heating and cooling, with only a slight deviation around ~600 °C attributed to possible dissolution of carbide and/or cementite.

The text describes the processing route as homogenization at 1100 °C for 2 hr, hot forging to 50% thickness reduction in 1050-800 °C with air cooling, and hot rolling (soaking 1100 °C, 2hr) in two passes of 50% reduction each followed by water quenching.

subfigures.description: Temperature vs Time process schematic after casting. Steps labelled: Homogenization at 1100 °C for 2hr; Hot forging followed by air cooling; Hot rolling at 1100 °C for 2hr (two passes with an intermediate reheating excursion), then water quenching; Intercritical Annealing at 750 °C for 5-180 Min followed by air cooling. Axes are labelled Temperature, °C (vertical) and Time (horizontal) with no numeric time scale.

Thermo-Calc equilibrium phase-fraction plot. y-axis 'Volume fraction of all phase' (0.0-1.0), x-axis 'Temperature (°C)' (ticks ~200 to 1600). Curves: BCC_A2 (teal) high at low temperature, minimum ~0.5 at ~900 °C, maximum ~0.95 just below 1400 °C then sharp drop; FCC_A1 (orange) hump peaking ~0.5-0.55 near 950-1000 °C; LIQUID (purple) rising steeply to 1.0 near 1500 °C; minor phases (KAPPA_E21, Cementite, M23C6, CUB_A13, FE8SI2C, CBCC_A12) stay near zero fraction and are hard to distinguish individually.

Dilatometry curve: 'Change in Length' (y, -50 to 200, no unit printed) vs Temperature (x, ticks ~200 to 1000 °C). Two essentially overlapping linear heating/cooling traces labelled '5 min. holding time' (black) and '15 min. holding time' (red); a black ellipse marks a small deviation/hump at ~600 °C. Both curves reach ~180 change-in-length near 1000-1050 °C.
